**1 — Scene:** A mixed vegetarian meal: apparent tofu, cauliflower, shredded vegetable slaw, and a reddish quinoa-and-vegetable mixture.

**2 — Vessel:** A large, rounded-square dinner plate, partly cropped. I’ll approximate it using a **27 cm equivalent diameter**: area = 3.14 × 13.5² ≈ **572 cm²**.

**3 — Items:** Pale seasoned tofu slices; cauliflower florets; cabbage, radish, and carrot slaw; quinoa with vegetables and reddish sauce. Light dressing/coating is included in the estimates below rather than counted separately.

**4–7 — Area, volume, weight, and energy:**

| Item | Plate area | Area × typical height = volume | Bulk density | Weight | kcal/100 g | Energy |
|---|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|---:|
| Seasoned tofu | 12% | 69 cm² × 1.4 cm = 97 ml | 0.95 | 92 g | 145 | 133 kcal |
| Cauliflower | 5% | 29 cm² × 1.3 cm = 38 ml | 0.60 | 23 g | 60 | 14 kcal |
| Lightly dressed vegetable slaw | 17% | 97 cm² × 1.2 cm = 116 ml | 0.60 | 70 g | 45 | 32 kcal |
| Quinoa, vegetables, and reddish sauce | 21% | 120 cm² × 1.7 cm = 204 ml | 0.80 | 163 g | 150 | 245 kcal |

The food areas total **55% of the plate**, leaving substantial empty space.

**8 — Sanity check:** Approximately **348 g and 424 kcal** is plausible for the visible portions. The main uncertainties are the quinoa mound’s depth and the amount of oil in the coatings.
